_meta.description: Triage evaluation scenarios for JARVIS Legal OS. Each has a hidden fact sheet (ground truth) and the expected triage output.

scenarios.opening_message: I got hurt at work and I don't know what to do.

hidden_facts.what_happened: Warehouse worker at Amazon fulfillment center in Staten Island. A forklift operated by a coworker backed into him, pinning his leg against a shelf. Broken tibia.
hidden_facts.where: Amazon fulfillment center, Staten Island, NY (Richmond County)
hidden_facts.harm: Broken tibia, 6 weeks out of work, $45,000 in medical bills
hidden_facts.documents: Incident report filed with employer, ER records from Richmond University Medical Center, photos of the scene
hidden_facts.actions_taken: Reported to supervisor same day. Filed employer incident report.

expected.court_or_agency: New York State Workers' Compensation Board
expected.urgency_reason: 30-day employer notice deadline, 2-year claim filing deadline
expected.notes: Purely WC — coworker caused it but both work for same employer. No third-party claim.

scenarios.opening_message: A truck hit me while I was working outside.

hidden_facts.what_happened: Construction worker for ABC Builders doing road work in the Bronx. A FedEx delivery truck ran a barricade and struck him. The FedEx driver was on duty.
hidden_facts.where: Grand Concourse and 161st Street, Bronx, NY (Bronx County)
hidden_facts.who: Employer: ABC Builders (construction company). Third party: FedEx driver (separate company).
hidden_facts.harm: Herniated discs L4-L5, shoulder tear. Out of work 3 months. $80,000+ medical bills.
hidden_facts.documents: Police report, employer incident report, MRI results, ambulance record
hidden_facts.actions_taken: Went to ER by ambulance. Employer filed WC report.

court_or_agency: New York State Workers' Compensation Board
expected.urgency_reason: Third-party tort claim has 3-year SOL but should act quickly to preserve evidence. WC has 30-day notice requirement.
expected.notes: Classic dual-track: WC against own employer + third-party tort against FedEx. Triage must identify both.

scenarios.opening_message: I slipped and fell and I think I broke something.

hidden_facts.what_happened: Office worker slipped on a freshly mopped floor in the lobby of her office building during work hours. The building is owned by a separate property management company, not her employer.
hidden_facts.where: 330 Madison Avenue, Manhattan, NY (New York County)
hidden_facts.who: Employer: Deloitte (tenant). Building owner: SL Green Realty (landlord/property manager).
hidden_facts.harm: Fractured wrist, 2 weeks out of work
hidden_facts.documents: Building security camera footage (requested), ER visit records, supervisor email acknowledging incident
hidden_facts.actions_taken: Reported to HR at Deloitte. Filed incident report with building management.

court_or_agency: New York State Workers' Compensation Board
expected.urgency_reason: WC 30-day notice done. Third-party premises liability against building owner has 3-year SOL.
expected.notes: WC against employer + premises liability tort against building owner. Triage must ask whether the slip happened in employer's space or common area, and who maintains it.

scenarios.opening_message: I fell down the stairs at a restaurant.

hidden_facts.what_happened: Customer (not an employee) slipped on wet stairs at a restaurant in Park Slope, Brooklyn. No 'wet floor' sign was posted.
hidden_facts.where: Restaurant on 5th Avenue, Park Slope, Brooklyn, NY (Kings County)
hidden_facts.harm: Sprained ankle, bruised ribs. ER visit, follow-up with orthopedist.
hidden_facts.documents: Photos of wet stairs (no sign), ER records, restaurant receipt showing she was there
hidden_facts.actions_taken: Took photos, got manager's name, went to ER

expected.urgency_reason: 3-year SOL for personal injury against private party. No notice of claim required.
expected.notes: Straightforward premises liability against private business. No WC — she's a customer.

scenarios.opening_message: My kid was hurt at school.

hidden_facts.what_happened: 8-year-old child fell off broken playground equipment at PS 123 in the Bronx. The school is a NYC public school (DOE).
hidden_facts.where: PS 123, Bronx, NY (Bronx County)
hidden_facts.who: NYC Department of Education / City of New York
hidden_facts.harm: Broken arm, surgery required. $25,000 in medical bills.
hidden_facts.documents: School nurse report, ER records, photos of broken equipment
hidden_facts.actions_taken: Took child to ER. Called the school principal.

expected.urgency_reason: 90-day Notice of Claim deadline. Incident was Sept 5 — deadline is approximately December 4, 2026. Only ~41 days remaining.
expected.notes: Tort against City of New York (DOE is a city agency). Must file Notice of Claim within 90 days. Triage must flag the urgency.

scenarios.opening_message: I was in a car accident on the highway.

hidden_facts.what_happened: Rear-ended by another driver on the Long Island Expressway near exit 39 in Suffolk County. The other driver was texting.
hidden_facts.where: Long Island Expressway, near exit 39, Dix Hills, Suffolk County, NY
hidden_facts.who: Other driver (private individual, has Geico insurance)
hidden_facts.harm: Whiplash, lower back pain. 3 chiropractic visits so far.
hidden_facts.documents: Police report (Suffolk County PD), insurance info exchanged, photos of damage, medical records
hidden_facts.actions_taken: Called police, exchanged info, filed claim with own insurance (no-fault)

expected.urgency_reason: 3-year SOL. No-fault threshold must be met for lawsuit. Should document injuries.
expected.notes: Standard motor vehicle accident. NY no-fault applies. Must meet serious injury threshold (Insurance Law 5102(d)) to sue for pain and suffering.

scenarios.opening_message: A delivery guy on an e-bike hit me while I was crossing the street.

hidden_facts.what_happened: Pedestrian struck by a DoorDash delivery cyclist on an electric bike running a red light at an intersection in Midtown Manhattan.
hidden_facts.where: 7th Avenue and 34th Street, Manhattan, NY (New York County)
hidden_facts.who: DoorDash delivery driver (gig worker, may be independent contractor)
hidden_facts.harm: Broken collarbone, road rash, concussion. 2 days in hospital.
hidden_facts.documents: Witness statements (2 bystanders), hospital records, police report
hidden_facts.actions_taken: Called 911, went to hospital by ambulance, police filed report

expected.urgency_reason: 3-year SOL. Question of whether DoorDash is vicariously liable for gig worker.
expected.notes: Tort against delivery driver and possibly DoorDash (respondeat superior / gig economy liability). Not WC — victim is pedestrian.

scenarios.opening_message: I think the doctor messed up my surgery.

hidden_facts.what_happened: Gallbladder removal surgery at NYU Langone. Surgeon accidentally nicked the common bile duct, requiring a second emergency surgery.
hidden_facts.where: NYU Langone Health, Manhattan, NY (New York County)
hidden_facts.who: Surgeon (Dr. at NYU Langone), hospital (NYU Langone)
hidden_facts.harm: Additional surgery, 3 extra weeks in hospital, ongoing digestive issues, $120,000 additional medical bills
hidden_facts.documents: Medical records, operative reports, second surgery records, bills
hidden_facts.actions_taken: Nothing yet. Just realized the complication was from surgical error after seeing another doctor.

expected.urgency_reason: Medical malpractice SOL is 2.5 years from the act (CPLR 214-a) with discovery rule complexities. July 2026 + 2.5 years = Jan 2029, but should act promptly for expert review.
expected.notes: Medical malpractice (subset of torts). Requires certificate of merit. 2.5-year SOL, not 3.

scenarios.opening_message: My neighbor's dog bit my hand pretty bad.

hidden_facts.what_happened: Neighbor's pit bull escaped their yard and bit the person on the hand and forearm while they were walking on the sidewalk.
hidden_facts.where: Residential street in Jamaica, Queens, NY (Queens County)
hidden_facts.harm: Deep puncture wounds, 12 stitches, possible nerve damage. Tetanus shot.
hidden_facts.documents: Animal control report, ER records, photos of injuries, neighbor's info
hidden_facts.actions_taken: Called 311 and animal control. Went to ER.

expected.urgency_reason: 3-year SOL. Evidence already documented.
expected.notes: Dog bite — strict liability if prior vicious propensity known, otherwise negligence.

scenarios.opening_message: I tripped on a broken sidewalk and now I can't walk right.

hidden_facts.what_happened: Tripped on a raised/cracked sidewalk section in front of a commercial building in Astoria, Queens. The sidewalk is a city sidewalk (NYC owns it, but abutting property owner may share liability under NYC Admin Code 7-210).
hidden_facts.where: Broadway near 30th Street, Astoria, Queens, NY (Queens County)
hidden_facts.who: City of New York and/or abutting property owner
hidden_facts.harm: Torn ACL, surgery needed. Out of work 8 weeks.
hidden_facts.documents: Photos of the cracked sidewalk, ER records, MRI showing ACL tear
hidden_facts.actions_taken: Went to ER. Took photos the next day.

expected.urgency_reason: 90-day Notice of Claim deadline. Incident Aug 28 — deadline ~Nov 26, 2026. About 33 days remaining.
expected.notes: Must file Notice of Claim against City of NY within 90 days. May also have claim against abutting property owner (private tort, 3-year SOL). Triage must flag the 90-day clock.

scenarios.opening_message: I was hurt during a delivery for my job. The building's elevator broke.

hidden_facts.what_happened: UPS driver making a delivery. Building freight elevator malfunctioned and dropped two floors while he was inside. Building owned by a private landlord, not by UPS.
hidden_facts.where: Commercial building, 23rd Street, Manhattan (New York County)
hidden_facts.who: Employer: UPS. Building owner: separate private company.
hidden_facts.harm: Compression fracture in spine, knee injury. 4 months out of work.
hidden_facts.documents: UPS incident report, building violation history (DOB), ER records, ambulance report
hidden_facts.actions_taken: Ambulance to Bellevue. UPS filed workers comp claim. Building manager gave a report.

court_or_agency: New York State Workers' Compensation Board
expected.urgency_reason: WC already filed. Third-party tort against building owner — 3-year SOL but elevator cases may involve building code violations (strict liability).
expected.notes: Dual track: WC against UPS + third-party premises liability/elevator liability against building owner.

scenarios.opening_message: I got electrocuted on a construction site.

hidden_facts.what_happened: Electrician's apprentice working on a new building construction site. Hit an exposed live wire that should have been de-energized. The general contractor (a different company) was responsible for the electrical lockout.
hidden_facts.where: Construction site, Long Island City, Queens (Queens County)
hidden_facts.who: Own employer: Ace Electric (subcontractor). General contractor: Turner Construction. Site owner: Tishman Speyer.
hidden_facts.harm: Electrical burns on hands and arms, cardiac arrhythmia, 10 days in hospital
hidden_facts.documents: OSHA report, ER records, employer incident report, photos of the site
hidden_facts.actions_taken: Hospitalized. Employer filed WC. OSHA investigated.

court_or_agency: New York State Workers' Compensation Board
expected.urgency_reason: NY Labor Law 240/241 (scaffold law) may apply — strict liability on GC and owner for construction site safety. WC already underway.
expected.notes: Construction accident — potential Labor Law 240/241 claim against GC and site owner (strict liability). Plus WC against own employer. Triage must identify the multi-party structure.

scenarios.opening_message: I hurt my back lifting boxes. My boss says it's not their problem.

hidden_facts.what_happened: Retail worker at a private clothing store. Hurt back lifting heavy inventory boxes. Employer (small business, 8 employees) denies it's work-related and refuses to file a WC claim.
hidden_facts.where: Clothing store, Fordham Road, Bronx, NY (Bronx County)
hidden_facts.harm: Herniated disc, can't stand for long periods. Lost wages from missed shifts.
hidden_facts.documents: Text messages with boss about the injury, urgent care records, no employer incident report
hidden_facts.actions_taken: Told boss verbally. Boss said 'not my problem.' Went to urgent care on own.

expected.court_or_agency: New York State Workers' Compensation Board
expected.urgency_reason: Must notify employer in writing within 30 days. Can file WC claim directly with WCB even if employer refuses. 2-year filing deadline.
expected.notes: Employer denial doesn't eliminate WC rights. Worker can file C-3 form directly with WCB. Triage should note the employer has 8 employees — WC is mandatory for nearly all NY employers.

scenarios.opening_message: I was attacked by a patient at the nursing home where I work.

hidden_facts.what_happened: Certified nursing assistant at a private nursing home. A dementia patient punched her in the face during care, breaking her nose. The facility had prior complaints about understaffing and violent patient incidents.
hidden_facts.where: Private nursing home, Yonkers, Westchester County, NY
hidden_facts.harm: Broken nose, emotional distress, 2 weeks out of work
hidden_facts.documents: Incident report at facility, ER records, prior OSHA complaints about facility
hidden_facts.actions_taken: Filed incident report with employer. Went to ER.

expected.court_or_agency: New York State Workers' Compensation Board
expected.urgency_reason: 30-day notice, 2-year filing deadline. Also may have employment safety complaint with OSHA.
expected.notes: WC claim. Can't sue employer directly (exclusive remedy). Can't sue the patient (dementia). Possible OSHA complaint about facility conditions but that doesn't give her money damages.

scenarios.opening_message: I got hurt on a scaffold and my boss told me not to report it.

hidden_facts.what_happened: Construction worker painting a building exterior. The scaffold was improperly secured and partially collapsed. He fell 8 feet. His employer told him to say he fell off a ladder at home.
hidden_facts.where: Residential building, Bay Ridge, Brooklyn (Kings County)
hidden_facts.who: Own employer: small painting contractor (5 workers). Building owner: private landlord.
hidden_facts.harm: Broken ankle, torn rotator cuff. Unable to work.
hidden_facts.documents: Photos from coworker's phone showing collapsed scaffold, ER records, text from boss telling him to lie
hidden_facts.actions_taken: Went to ER. Did NOT file with employer (afraid of retaliation).

court_or_agency: New York State Workers' Compensation Board
expected.urgency_reason: Labor Law 240 scaffold law applies (strict liability on building owner). WC 30-day notice clock running. Employer retaliation is illegal under WCL 120.
expected.notes: Scaffold collapse = Labor Law 240 strict liability against building owner. WC against employer. Employer telling worker to lie is a separate violation. Must file WC notice despite employer pressure.

scenarios.opening_message: I was in a rideshare and we got rear-ended.

hidden_facts.what_happened: Passenger in an Uber. Another car rear-ended the Uber at a red light. The Uber driver was not at fault.
hidden_facts.where: Atlantic Avenue and Flatbush Avenue, Brooklyn (Kings County)
hidden_facts.who: Uber driver, other driver (at-fault), their insurance companies
hidden_facts.harm: Neck pain, headaches. Went to urgent care.
hidden_facts.documents: Uber trip receipt, police report, urgent care records, photos of damage
hidden_facts.actions_taken: Called police. Got Uber trip info from app. Went to urgent care next day.

expected.urgency_reason: 3-year SOL. No-fault applies. Should document injuries.
expected.notes: Passenger in rideshare — not WC (not working). Tort claim against at-fault driver. Uber has $1M liability policy for passengers. No-fault threshold applies for pain/suffering claim.

scenarios.opening_message: Lead paint is making my kids sick.

hidden_facts.what_happened: Children (ages 3 and 5) have elevated blood lead levels. Family lives in a pre-1978 apartment in the Bronx. Landlord was notified of peeling paint 6 months ago and did nothing. NYC requires landlords to remediate lead in apartments with children under 6.
hidden_facts.where: Apartment building, Tremont, Bronx (Bronx County)
hidden_facts.who: Landlord (private). NYC HPD (Housing Preservation and Development) for enforcement.
hidden_facts.harm: Elevated blood lead levels in both children. Potential developmental harm.
hidden_facts.documents: Blood test results, pediatrician letters, photos of peeling paint, prior complaints to landlord (text messages), HPD complaint number
hidden_facts.actions_taken: Called 311 and filed HPD complaint. Landlord did nothing.

expected.urgency_reason: Ongoing health hazard to young children. Lead paint tort has 3-year SOL from discovery. Housing code violations enforceable immediately.
expected.notes: Dual: tort for lead poisoning damages + housing court for code enforcement. NYC Local Law 1 (lead paint). Misleading opener — sounds like housing but is also a major tort.

scenarios.opening_message: I slipped on ice outside my apartment building.

hidden_facts.what_happened: Slipped on ice on the sidewalk directly in front of their apartment building. Landlord had not salted or cleared snow/ice. Building is a privately owned walk-up.
hidden_facts.where: Apartment building sidewalk, Bushwick, Brooklyn (Kings County)
hidden_facts.harm: Hip fracture. Surgery, 6 weeks recovery, physical therapy ongoing.
hidden_facts.documents: Photos of icy sidewalk, weather records showing snowfall, ER and surgical records, PT records

expected.urgency_reason: 3-year SOL from Jan 15, 2026 = Jan 15, 2029. Ample time but should act. NYC Admin Code 7-210 makes property owner liable for sidewalk maintenance.
expected.notes: Premises liability — private landlord. NYC Admin Code 7-210 shifted sidewalk liability to abutting property owners. Not a city claim.

scenarios.opening_message: My car got totaled but I wasn't hurt. The other guy had no insurance.

hidden_facts.what_happened: T-boned at an intersection by an uninsured driver who ran a stop sign. Person's car is totaled ($15,000 value). Person has uninsured motorist coverage on their own policy.
hidden_facts.where: Intersection in New Rochelle, Westchester County, NY
hidden_facts.harm: No personal injury. $15,000 property damage. Rental car costs.
hidden_facts.documents: Police report, photos of damage, own insurance policy, repair estimate
hidden_facts.actions_taken: Filed police report. Called own insurance.

expected.court_or_agency: City Court or Small Claims (New Rochelle)
expected.urgency_reason: 3-year SOL. Property damage only. UM/SUM claim on own policy may cover it.
expected.notes: Property damage only — no personal injury tort per se, but still a tort (property damage). Uninsured motorist claim through own policy. If policy doesn't cover fully, small claims or city court against driver (likely uncollectible).

scenarios.opening_message: I got food poisoning from a restaurant and I was in the hospital for three days.

hidden_facts.what_happened: Ate at a restaurant in Manhattan. Within 6 hours developed severe vomiting and diarrhea. Diagnosed with salmonella. Hospitalized for 3 days. NYC Health Department later confirmed a salmonella outbreak linked to the restaurant.
hidden_facts.where: Restaurant in Chelsea, Manhattan (New York County)
hidden_facts.harm: Severe salmonella infection, 3-day hospitalization, 2 weeks recovery, $18,000 medical bills, lost wages
hidden_facts.documents: Hospital records showing salmonella diagnosis, NYC Health Department outbreak report (public record), restaurant receipt
hidden_facts.actions_taken: Went to ER. Called 311 to report.

expected.urgency_reason: 3-year SOL. Health department report provides strong evidence.
expected.notes: Products liability / negligence tort against restaurant. NYC Health Dept outbreak confirmation is strong evidence.

scenarios.opening_message: A store security guard tackled me and I wasn't even stealing anything.

hidden_facts.what_happened: Falsely accused of shoplifting at a department store. Security guard physically tackled and restrained the person in front of other customers. Person was handcuffed by guard until police arrived. Police found no stolen items and let person go. No arrest made.
hidden_facts.where: Department store in Herald Square, Manhattan (New York County)
hidden_facts.who: Department store (private business), security guard (employee of store or contract security company)
hidden_facts.harm: Shoulder injury from tackle, humiliation, emotional distress
hidden_facts.documents: Police report (no arrest), ER records, store surveillance footage (should be preserved), witness names

expected.urgency_reason: 3-year SOL. Should preserve surveillance footage quickly — stores overwrite.
expected.notes: False imprisonment, assault/battery, possibly civil rights. Private actor — not 1983. Could also be defamation.

scenarios.opening_message: I was exposed to asbestos at my old job and now I have a lung problem.

hidden_facts.what_happened: Worked in building demolition from 1995-2010. Recently diagnosed with mesothelioma. Multiple employers over the years, several are now defunct.
hidden_facts.where: Various sites across NYC and Long Island
hidden_facts.who: Multiple former employers (some defunct), building owners, asbestos product manufacturers
hidden_facts.harm: Mesothelioma diagnosis. Terminal illness.
hidden_facts.documents: Medical records and diagnosis, employment records, Social Security work history
hidden_facts.actions_taken: Nothing legal yet. Just got the diagnosis.

expected.urgency_reason: Mesothelioma is terminal. Discovery rule applies for SOL. Expedited trial scheduling available in NY for asbestos cases (NYCAL). Must act immediately.
expected.notes: Asbestos tort — specialized area. NY has NYCAL (NYC Asbestos Litigation) in Supreme Court, NY County. Discovery rule for SOL. Multiple defendants likely. Asbestos trust funds also available.

scenarios.opening_message: I fell at work but I think the building is also at fault. I'm undocumented — do I still have rights?

hidden_facts.what_happened: Undocumented worker employed as a janitor. Fell down stairs in a commercial building because the stairwell light was out and handrail was broken. The building is owned by a separate management company.
hidden_facts.where: Commercial building, Jackson Heights, Queens (Queens County)
hidden_facts.who: Employer: cleaning company. Building owner: separate management company.
hidden_facts.harm: Fractured vertebra, concussion. Unable to work.
hidden_facts.documents: ER records (under his real name), photos of dark stairwell and broken handrail
hidden_facts.actions_taken: Went to ER. Afraid to report because of immigration status.

court_or_agency: New York State Workers' Compensation Board
expected.urgency_reason: WC 30-day notice clock running. Immigration status does NOT bar WC or tort claims in NY. Must act quickly.
expected.notes: Immigration status is irrelevant for WC and tort claims in NY. Triage must reassure but not give advice. Dual track: WC + third-party tort against building owner.

scenarios.opening_message: My coworker keeps groping me and my boss won't do anything. Yesterday he shoved me and I hit my head.

hidden_facts.what_happened: Ongoing sexual harassment by coworker at a restaurant. Yesterday the coworker physically shoved her into a wall, causing a head injury. She reported to the manager weeks ago about the groping; manager said 'deal with it.' Employer has 20 employees.
hidden_facts.where: Restaurant in Williamsburg, Brooklyn (Kings County)
hidden_facts.when: Harassment ongoing for 2 months. Physical assault: October 23, 2026.
hidden_facts.who: Coworker (harasser/assailant), employer (restaurant, 20 employees), manager (failed to act)
hidden_facts.harm: Concussion from the shove, emotional distress from ongoing harassment, missed work
hidden_facts.documents: Text messages to manager reporting harassment, ER records for concussion, names of witnesses
hidden_facts.actions_taken: Reported to manager (ignored). Went to ER after the shove.

court_or_agency: New York State Workers' Compensation Board
expected.urgency_reason: Physical safety at risk. Assault is also a crime — can file police report. WC for the head injury. Employment discrimination claim (sexual harassment). Civil tort for assault.
expected.notes: Multi-faceted: employment discrimination (sexual harassment), WC for the physical injury, tort (assault/battery) against coworker, criminal complaint. Triage must flag safety first.

scenarios.opening_message: I got carbon monoxide poisoning in my apartment.

hidden_facts.what_happened: Faulty boiler in apartment building caused carbon monoxide leak. Person and two roommates hospitalized. Building is privately owned, 12-unit apartment.
hidden_facts.where: Apartment building, Prospect Heights, Brooklyn (Kings County)
hidden_facts.who: Landlord/building owner (private), possibly boiler maintenance company
hidden_facts.harm: CO poisoning — headaches, nausea, memory issues. 2-day hospitalization.
hidden_facts.documents: Hospital records, FDNY report confirming CO source as boiler, HPD complaint, photos
hidden_facts.actions_taken: Called 911. FDNY responded. HPD complaint filed.

expected.urgency_reason: Ongoing safety hazard. Tort claim (3-year SOL). Housing code violations for immediate enforcement.
expected.notes: Dual: tort for personal injury from CO poisoning + housing code enforcement. FDNY report is strong evidence. May also have claim against boiler maintenance company.

scenarios.opening_message: I think I have a repetitive stress injury from typing all day at work.

hidden_facts.what_happened: Office worker at an insurance company. Developed severe carpal tunnel syndrome over 2 years of constant typing. Doctor says it's work-related. Employer provided no ergonomic equipment.
hidden_facts.where: Insurance company office, White Plains, Westchester County, NY
hidden_facts.harm: Carpal tunnel syndrome both wrists. Needs surgery. Reduced grip strength.
hidden_facts.documents: Doctor's note stating work-related, MRI results, employment records showing job duties
hidden_facts.actions_taken: Told HR. HR said to 'see your own doctor.'

expected.court_or_agency: New York State Workers' Compensation Board
expected.urgency_reason: Occupational disease — 2-year filing deadline from date of disablement or date worker knew/should have known it was work-related. Must file C-3 form with WCB.
expected.notes: WC occupational disease claim. No third-party tort (employer's own premises/equipment). Filing deadline is 2 years from date of disablement.

scenarios.opening_message: A ceiling tile fell on my head while I was shopping.

hidden_facts.what_happened: In a big-box retail store (Home Depot), a ceiling tile and part of the suspended ceiling frame fell, striking the person on the head and shoulder.
hidden_facts.where: Home Depot, Whitestone, Queens (Queens County)
hidden_facts.harm: Concussion, shoulder bruise. ER visit.
hidden_facts.documents: Store incident report, ER records, photos of fallen ceiling debris, witness contact info
hidden_facts.actions_taken: Filled out store incident report. Went to ER.

expected.urgency_reason: 3-year SOL. Evidence already documented.
expected.notes: Premises liability against store. Private business — no notice of claim needed.

scenarios.opening_message: I was a passenger on a county bus that crashed.

hidden_facts.what_happened: Passenger on a Westchester Bee-Line bus. Bus driver ran a red light and collided with another vehicle. Passenger was thrown forward.
hidden_facts.where: Route 20 bus, Yonkers, Westchester County, NY
hidden_facts.who: Westchester County (operates Bee-Line bus system through contractor)
hidden_facts.harm: Neck injury, back pain. ER visit and ongoing PT.
hidden_facts.documents: Bus incident number, police report, ER records, photos of injuries
hidden_facts.actions_taken: Gave info to police at scene. Went to ER.

expected.urgency_reason: Claim against county = Notice of Claim required within 90 days. Incident Oct 12 — deadline ~Jan 10, 2027.
expected.notes: Bee-Line is a county-operated system — Notice of Claim required against Westchester County, not NYC Comptroller. Different entity than MTA.

scenarios.opening_message: I was hurt playing in a recreational soccer league organized by my company.

hidden_facts.what_happened: Company-organized recreational soccer league on weekends. Twisted knee badly during a game. Employer (a tech company) organized and paid for the league but participation was voluntary and games were on Saturdays.
hidden_facts.where: Soccer field, Randall's Island, Manhattan (New York County)
hidden_facts.who: Employer organized the league but it was voluntary weekend activity
hidden_facts.harm: Torn meniscus. Needs surgery.
hidden_facts.documents: Email from employer organizing the league, ER records, MRI results
hidden_facts.actions_taken: Went to ER. Told boss on Monday.

expected.court_or_agency: New York State Workers' Compensation Board
expected.urgency_reason: WC coverage is arguable — depends on whether participation was truly voluntary or implicitly expected. 30-day notice, 2-year filing deadline.
expected.unknown: Whether the activity qualifies as in the course of employment. Key factors: was attendance expected? Did employer pay? Was it during work hours?
expected.notes: Borderline WC case. NY courts have found WC coverage for employer-sponsored recreational activities if employer benefited and participation was encouraged. Triage should identify the uncertainty.

scenarios.opening_message: Someone pushed me onto the tracks at a train station.

hidden_facts.what_happened: Pushed onto the train tracks by a stranger at a LIRR station. Fell onto the trackbed. Another passenger pulled them up before the train arrived. The attacker fled.
hidden_facts.where: LIRR station, Jamaica, Queens (Queens County)
hidden_facts.who: Unknown attacker (stranger). LIRR (possible negligent security claim).
hidden_facts.harm: Fractured wrist from fall, severe emotional trauma, PTSD symptoms
hidden_facts.documents: LIRR incident report, police report, ER records, station camera footage (should be preserved)
hidden_facts.actions_taken: Called 911. Police and EMS responded. Filed police report.

expected.urgency_reason: LIRR is an MTA entity — requires Notice of Claim within 90 days against a public authority. Criminal investigation ongoing.
expected.notes: Tort against LIRR for negligent security (should have had adequate security/barriers). Criminal assault by stranger (NYPD investigating). Dual civil/criminal. Must file Notice of Claim against LIRR.

scenarios.opening_message: My landlord is trying to kick me out.

hidden_facts.what_happened: Landlord served a 14-day rent demand notice, claiming $3,200 in back rent. Tenant disputes the amount — says they paid in cash and landlord didn't give receipts. Rent-stabilized apartment.
hidden_facts.where: Apartment in Washington Heights, Manhattan (New York County)
hidden_facts.harm: Potential eviction, housing instability
hidden_facts.documents: 14-day rent demand notice, lease, bank statements showing cash withdrawals matching rent, text messages about payments

expected.urgency_reason: 14-day demand is a prerequisite to eviction proceeding. If not resolved, landlord can file in Housing Court. Tenant should respond and gather proof of payment.

scenarios.opening_message: I got papers from a court about my apartment.

hidden_facts.what_happened: Served with a Petition and Notice of Petition for a holdover proceeding. Landlord claims lease expired and was not renewed. Tenant has lived there 15 years in a rent-stabilized unit and believes they have a right to renewal.
hidden_facts.where: Apartment in Flatbush, Brooklyn (Kings County)
hidden_facts.harm: Facing eviction
hidden_facts.documents: Notice of Petition, Petition (holdover), current and prior leases, rent receipts

expected.urgency_reason: Court date in ~17 days. Must answer or appear. Rent stabilization provides strong renewal rights.

scenarios.opening_message: My heat hasn't worked for two weeks and it's getting cold.

hidden_facts.what_happened: No heat in the apartment since October 10. Landlord not responsive. Heat season in NYC starts October 1. Multiple tenants affected.
hidden_facts.where: Apartment building, East Harlem, Manhattan (New York County)
hidden_facts.harm: Unsafe living conditions, especially for elderly tenant on 4th floor
hidden_facts.documents: Text messages to landlord, 311 complaint confirmation, indoor temperature photos
